Find the arc length of the polar curve $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta $ for $\frac{3\pi }{2}\le \theta \le \frac{7\pi }{4}$ (shown in blue in the diagram above).
worked_solution:
The arc length $L$ of a polar curve $r=r(\theta )$ is given by

$$
L={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta .
$$

Since $r=2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta ,$ we have

$$
\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta }=-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta .
$$

Therefore, the arc length is

$$
\begin{aligned}L & ={\int }_{{\theta }_{1}}^{{\theta }_{2}}\sqrt{{r}^{2}+{(\frac{\text{d}r}{\text{d}\theta })}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{3\pi /2}^{7\pi /4}\sqrt{(2\operatorname{cos}⁡\theta )^{2}+{(-2\operatorname{sin}⁡\theta )}^{2}}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & ={\int }_{3\pi /2}^{7\pi /4}\sqrt{4({cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta )}\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2{\int }_{3\pi /2}^{7\pi /4}1\,\text{d}\theta  \\  & =2\theta {|}_{3\pi /2}^{7\pi /4} \\  & =2(\frac{7\pi }{4}-\frac{3\pi }{2}) \\  & =\frac{\pi }{2}.\end{aligned}
$$
